chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Kunanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of a pregnant woman is one (revocation), and her waiting period is the nearer of the two periods.

key_terms.أَقْرَبُ الْأَجَلَيْنِ: The nearer of the two periods
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One (referring to a single revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a pregnant woman who is divorced according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a pregnant woman’s ʿiddah concludes upon childbirth, aligning with the Quranic principle of 'whichever comes first' (aqrab al-ajalayn). This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for determining the finality of divorce and the mother's eligibility to remarry, emphasizing the unique physiological status of pregnancy as a distinct waiting period separate from the standard three-month or menstrual cycle durations.
